title: Attention kernel priority decider and quantization-impact audit for prefill+decode
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Problem: Over the last month we've seen intermittent latency regressions and memory pressure spikes on prefill-heavy traffic profiles when upgrading some clusters to FlashAttention v3 (FAv3). The regressions are most pronounced for quantized model variants (4-bit and mixed-int8) during medium batch prefill (batch=3..6) and long-context runs (>4k tokens). Root cause hypotheses include: FAv3 kernel choice at runtime mismatches workload shape, increased temporary memory allocations in specific kernel variants, and a mismatch between prefill and decode kernel preferences that causes cache fragmentation and CPU-GPU sync jitter. Goals: 1) Implement a lightweight kernel "priority decider" that scores candidate attention kernels per-request using features (seq_len, batch, kv_cache_size, quant_mode, available_memory_bytes, historical-latency-percentiles). 2) Run a focused quantization-impact audit across representative models (gpt-like 1B, 7B, 13B) to capture latency/cost/reliability delta between FAv2/FAv3 and fallback kernels. 3) Add telemetry and per-request annotations so we can A/B canary kernel policies and finely roll back for high-risk customers. 4) Produce a rollout plan with automatic rollback and canary percentages.
acceptance_criteria: A kernel priority decider component exists in the runtime that returns a ranked list of kernel candidates for a request
Decision factors include at minimum: seq_len, batch_size, kv_cache_bytes, quant_mode, gpu_free_bytes, and historic p95 latency for the model+shape
Microbenchmarks: documented latency and memory profiles for FAv2, FAv3, and fallback kernels across selected shapes and quantization modes with clear pass/fail thresholds
Telemetry: traces include selected kernel id, reason score breakdown, and whether a fallback occurred; data ingested into console dashboards
Canary rollout plan defined and implemented: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback condition based on error/latency SLOs
Runbook updated and an incident drill scheduled to validate fallback procedures
updates: 2026-03-10: Initial investigation — reproduced a 7-12% median latency regression on prefill for quantized 7B models on a4-gpu nodes when using FAv3 kernels with batch=4 and seq_len=4096. Memory high-water mark increased ~180MB compared to FAv2.

2026-03-11: Profiling discovered that one FAv3 variant performs an extra temporary allocation during softmax path for certain head/kv sizes; added a microbench harness to isolate the allocate-free path. Started drafting the priority scorer formula.

2026-03-12: Bench harness results: for 13B quantized at batch=2 seq=8192 FAv3 is 9% faster than fallback in pure decode but 11% slower on prefill due to prefilling memory churn. Created draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289 with harness and baseline CSVs.

2026-03-13: Decision: implement two-tier policy — (A) a lightweight scorer used in production to pick kernels, (B) a conservative prefill override that favors allocation-stable kernels when kv_cache_bytes > threshold. Added telemetry fields kernel_priority_score and prefill_override to trace schema. Opened canary plan doc and flagged rollback thresholds.

Next steps: land scorer proto in runtime (ENG-38907-scoring-wip branch), run full quantization-impact audit across customer-shaped workloads (tickets to schedule with Solutions), prepare console dashboard widgets for kernel-level p95/p99 latencies.
